name: Condition tree
reader_question: Which sequence of conditions leads to each outcome, and where does a given case end up?
relationship: Hierarchical decision structure: condition nodes with named branches terminating in outcomes.
use_when: Eligibility or applicability is decided by successive tests
Each test has a small set of named answers and every answer ends in an outcome
avoid_when: Several criteria are weighed together rather than in sequence — use criterion-matrix
Conditions can combine in any order — use a table of rules

data_contract.notes: The first node is the root
Every condition names at least two distinct branches; each target is declared and has one parent
Outcome whose route from the root is drawn in the accent

units: No quantities; branch labels are answers such as Yes and No.

editable: Condition and outcome boxes, elbow lines and branch labels as native shapes and text
not_data_bound: The tree is drawn shapes with computed positions, not a SmartArt or data-bound object
Elbow lines are separate segments, not PowerPoint connectors

table_alternative: A rules table (route, conditions met, outcome).
variations: Vertical top-down layout for narrow panels
Branch frequencies where a source reports them
limitations: Depth is capped at four tests and nine outcomes
Branch labels must be short; long answers belong in the node text
A node reached by two branches is not a tree and is rejected

excluded_alternatives.reason: A tree has no cycles; loops describe processes, which state-diagram covers
Hides the order in which the tests apply
